name: powershell
description: Execute a Windows PowerShell command and stream its stdout. Hard cap 10 minutes per call; default 60s. Use this for anything you'd normally do in a Windows terminal: file ops, registry queries, service control, package management, network diagnostics, etc. Cancellation / timeout both kill the running PowerShell process — there is no orphan child after the call returns.

command.description: The exact PowerShell expression to run. Passed verbatim to `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command -`, so stdin-quoting rules apply (use double-quoted strings, escape embedded double quotes as `""`). Cannot be empty.

timeout.description: Maximum wall-clock seconds to wait for the command to finish. Required. Default 60, hard cap 600. The PowerShell process is killed if this elapses before the command returns.
